aliases: amorphous hybrid tungsten oxide-nickel hydroxide nanosheets

nodes.name: Hydrothermal WO3 synthesis
nodes.procedure: Na2WO4·2H2O (1.320 g, 4 mmol) was dissolved in 20 mL of H2O under stirring, and then 20 mL of acetic acid was added dropwise into the Na2WO4 solution. The tungstate was quickly hydrolyzed to form a milky white colloidal solution of hydrated tungsten oxides as a result of the decrease in pH. Then, the colloidal solution was transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave. Afterward, several pieces of cleaned and dried NF with an exposed geometrical area of 1 cm × 3 cm and one side covered by polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tape were immersed into the reaction solution in the autoclave, and then the autoclave was sealed and maintained at 180°C for 12 h. After the autoclave was cooled to ambient temperature naturally, the WO3·0.5H2O-WO3/NF products were removed from the autoclave and subsequently washed three times alternatively with ethanol and water at 50°C to purify the obtained products. Ultimately, the products were dried under a vacuum at 60°C overnight.
nodes.source_text: Typically, Na2WO4·2H2O (1.320 g, 4 mmol) was dissolved in 20 mL of H2O... dried under a vacuum at 60°C overnight

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Ni phosphate
nodes.procedure: Ni(H2O)6NH4PO4 was electrodeposited on WO3·0.5H2O-WO3/NF using a WaveDriver 20 Bundle electrochemical station by a potentiodynamic method at ambient temperature. The electrodeposition experiments were performed in a conventional three-electrode cell, composed of a WO3·0.5H2O-WO3/NF working electrode, a Ag/AgCl reference electrode (with saturated KCl solution), and a graphite rod counter electrode. The Ni(H2O)6NH4PO4 overlayer was cathodically deposited by cycling the WO3·0.5H2O-WO3/NF electrode between -1.34 and -0.55 V vs. Ag/AgCl at a scan rate of 20 mV·s⁻¹ for 200 cycles in 100 mL of an electrolyte solution (pH = 6.0) containing NiCl2·6H2O (29.71 g·L⁻¹), Na3(C3H5O7)·2H2O (20.00 g·L⁻¹), and (NH4)2HPO4 (13.33 g·L⁻¹).
nodes.source_text: Ni(H2O)6NH4PO4 was first electrodeposited on WO3·0.5H2O-WO3/NF... in 100 mL of an electrolyte solution (pH = 6.0)

nodes.name: NaOH chemical etching
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared Ni(H2O)6NH4PO4/WO3·0.5H2O-WO3/NF was immersed in 20 mL of an aqueous solution of NaOH (5 M) for 2 h at ambient temperature.
nodes.source_text: The as-prepared Ni(H2O)6NH4PO4/WO3·0.5H2O-WO3/NF was immersed in 20 mL of an aqueous solution of NaOH (5 M) for 2 h

nodes.name: Potentiodynamic activation
nodes.procedure: The resulting a-[WO3/Ni(OH)2]·0.2H2O/NF electrodes were obtained by cycling the (W,Ni)(O,OH)3/NF precursor between -0.05 and -0.450 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) at a scan rate of 20 mV·s⁻¹ for 200 cycles in an argon saturated aqueous solution of NaOH (1 M).
nodes.source_text: The resulting a-[WO3/Ni(OH)2]·0.2H2O/NF electrodes were obtained by cycling the (W,Ni)(O,OH)3/NF precursor between -0.05 and -0.450 V vs. RHE

aliases: amorphous hybrid tungsten oxide-nickel hydroxide nanosheets

nodes.characterization_summary: Overview, medium-, and high-magnification SEM images show NF skeletal surface homogeneously covered with dense, rough, multilayered structure featuring erected monolithic nanoridges in crisscross pattern and stacked submicrospheres (200-600 nm diameter) with hairy surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The overview scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image in Fig. 2(a) unambiguously illustrates that the skeletal surface of NF is homogeneously covered with dense, rough, multilayered (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃. A closer inspection of the rough features in high-magnification SEM images reveals a large number of erected monolithic nanoridges arranged in a crisscross pattern and interspersed with numerous stacked (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ submicrospheres with a diameter of 200-600 nm and a very hairy surface (Figs. 2(b) and 2(c)).

properties.description: Scanning Electron Microscopy image showing porous, nanostructured material with irregular, rough surface morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms cubic (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ phase with lattice constant a = 10.262 Å (space group: Fm3m(225)), matching ferritungstite structure with no impurity peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon etching with NaOH for 2h, the initial Ni(H₂O)₆NH₄PO₄/WO₃·0.5H₂O - WO₃ is completely transformed to cubic (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ phase with a lattice constant of a = 10.262Å (space group: Fm3m(225)), as revealed by the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern in Fig. 2(d).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDX shows average near-surface Ni/W/O atomic ratio of 4.55:1:16.57 with relatively uniform distribution of Ni, W, and O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The near-surface chemical composition of (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃/NF is evaluated by quantitative SEM-energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy analysis... The average near-surface Ni/W/O atomic ratio is 4.55:1:16.57.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals nanoridges and submicrospheres consist of ultrathin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging further reveals that both the nanoridges and submicrospheres consist of ultrathin nanosheets (Fig. 2(e)).

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing intricate network of thin, curved nanofilaments or nanoribbons with high surface area morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with d-spacings of 2.360 Å and 1.351 Å matching (331) and (731) planes of cubic ferritungstite phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image of (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ peeled off from NF... unveils the unambiguous lattice fringes with d-spacings of 2.360 and 1.351 Å, matching well with the (331) and (731) planes of the cubic ferritungstite phase.

properties.description: Inset showing selected area with clear lattice fringes indicating crystallinity

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDX confirms even distribution of Ni, W, and O elements with bulk Ni/W/O ratio of 4.55:1:16.78 and Ni/W ratio of 4.33:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average bulk composition of (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ is further analyzed by high-angle annular dark field (HAADF)-scanning TEM (STEM)-EDX elemental mapping... The quantitative STEM-EDX and ICP-OES analyses indicate that the average bulk Ni/W/O and Ni/W atomic ratios are 4.55:1:16.78 and 4.33:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows Ni³⁺ (856.0/873.8 eV) as predominant and Ni⁴⁺ (857.9/876.6 eV) as trace; W 4f shows W⁵⁺ and W⁶⁺ species associated with O²⁻/OH⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p core-level spectrum in Fig. 2(h) shows... peaks centered at binding energies (BEs) of 856.0 and 873.8 eV... attributed to the Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ from Ni³⁺ species... The deconvolution of W 4f core-level spectrum in Fig. 2(i) yields... W⁵⁺ ions... W⁶⁺ ions.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows no Bragg reflection peaks from a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O except NF substrate signals, confirming amorphous nature due to electrochemical reduction of Ni³⁺ to Ni²⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern in Fig. 4(a) shows the structural changes of the (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ precursor following the potential cycling under the HER conditions. Except the diffraction signals of NF, no Bragg reflection peaks from the resulting active material can be found due to the amorphous nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-magnification SEM shows rippling, crumpling, and porous ultrathin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-magnification SEM images in Figs. 4(b) and 4(c) illustrate the formation of the rippling, crumpling, and porous ultrathin nanosheets.

properties.features: nanofibrous morphology, porous network, highlighted inset region

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms porous ultrathin nanosheets with thickness of ca. 0.25-0.6 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) images further consolidate the porous and ultrathin features of all the nanosheets with an ultrasmall thickness of ca. 0.25-0.6 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms amorphous ultrathin nanosheets become fluffy and porous.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images further confirm that the amorphous ultrathin nanosheets becomes fluffy and porous relative to the compact precursor (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ nanosheets (Fig. 4(e)).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows amorphous concentric diffusion rings confirming low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding SAED pattern clearly exhibits amorphous concentric diffusion rings due to the low crystallinity of the resulting nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays considerably disordered lattice fringes confirming limited crystallinity with minor WO₃ domains.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image in Fig. 4(f) displays the considerably disordered lattice fringes, further confirming the limited crystallinity of the resulting nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDX shows relatively uniform elemental distribution of Ni, W, O with Ni/W/O ratios of 5.03:1:18.48 and Ni/W of 5.10:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The relatively uniform elemental distribution of Ni, W, and O throughout a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O nanosheets is also demonstrated... The quantitative STEM-EDX and ICP-OES analyses give the average bulk Ni/W/O and Ni/W atomic ratios of 5.03:1:18.48 and 5.10:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows dominant Ni²⁺ in Ni(OH)₂ (854.8/872.5 eV), minor Ni³⁺ in NiOOH (856.8/874.9 eV); W 4f similar to precursor but with slight BE shifts indicating electron transfer from Ni to W.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p core level spectrum can be fitted into two sets of doublets, of which one set consisting of two peaks at 854.8 (Ni 2p₃/₂) and 872.5 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂) can be readily assigned to the dominant Ni²⁺ ions in Ni(OH)₂... The W 4f core-level spectrum of a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O in Fig. 3(c) is analogous to that of (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows absorption edge at 8343.5 eV for (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ (Ni³⁺) shifting to 8341.9 eV for a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O (Ni²⁺) confirming reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge XANES spectra in Fig. 3(a) illustrate that the absorption edge (8343.5 eV) of (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ shows a 4.7 or 1.4 eV shift... Furthermore, the edge shift (8341.9 eV) of the a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O is similar to that (8342.1 eV) of the NiO specimen.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots fitted with equivalent circuit show charge transfer resistance R_ct = 0.99 Ω·cm² and series resistance R_s = 1.22 Ω·cm², indicating superior charge-transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The R_ct value of the a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O (0.99Ω·cm²) is much smaller than those of the a-WO₃ (2.58Ω), Ni(OH)₂ (3.03Ω·cm²), and NF (11.35Ω·cm²)... the lower series resistances (R_s) of the a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O (1.22Ω·cm²).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measurements yield double-layer capacitance C_dl of 3.38 mF·cm⁻² for ECSA estimation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl values are 3.38, 3.48, and 2.94 mF·cm⁻² for the a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O, a-WO₃, and Ni(OH)₂, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms bulk Ni/W atomic ratio of 4.33:1 for (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ and 5.10:1 for a-[WO₃/Ni(OH)₂]·0.2H₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The quantitative STEM-EDX and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analyses indicate that the average bulk Ni/W/O and Ni/W atomic ratios are 4.55:1:16.78 and 4.33:1, respectively... The quantitative STEM-EDX and ICP-OES analyses give the average bulk Ni/W/O and Ni/W atomic ratios of 5.03:1:18.48 and 5.10:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES absorption edge at 8343.5 eV (shifted 4.7 eV from Ni metal, 1.4 eV from NiO) confirms predominant Ni³⁺ (~+3.0) oxidation state in (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge XANES spectra in Fig. 3(a) illustrate that the absorption edge (8343.5 eV) of (W,Ni)(O,OH)₃ shows a 4.7 or 1.4 eV shift to higher energy with respect to that of metallic Ni (8338.8 eV) or NiO (8342.1 eV), respectively, revealing a much higher oxidation state than the Ni⁰ in Ni foil and even the Ni²⁺ in NiO.
